title: 📖 02｜Core Text Reading · Alsace
text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/40617d16de4c819db438c5fa47ea166f as of 2026-10-27T10:14:46.958Z: {"title":"02｜Core Text Reading · Alsace"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"📖"} Core Text Reading · Alsace
这一页只承担 Reading：让学生按教材逻辑读懂 Alsace。理解延伸、producer deep dive、额外地图与 further reading 留到下一轮。 ## 1｜Where Alsace Is Alsace 位于法国东北部，紧邻德国与瑞士。葡萄园沿 Vosges Mountains 东侧山麓呈狭长分布，Rhine River 构成重要地理背景。 ### Reading focus - Vosges Mountains = climatic barrier - Rhine Valley = regional geography - Haut-Rhin / Bas-Rhin = core administrative-geographic distinction ## 2｜Climate Vosges 形成明显 rain shadow，使 Alsace 在法国属于相对干燥、日照充足的葡萄酒区。整体为 continental / semi-continental climate，冬季寒冷，夏季温暖干燥，秋季成熟期通常较长。 ### What to understand while reading “北纬较高”并不自动等于“葡萄难成熟”。Alsace 的关键是 rain shadow + sunshine + slope exposure + long autumn。 ## 3｜Geology & Soils Alsace 位于 Rhine Graben 地质体系边缘，地质断裂与侵蚀造成极高的土壤多样性。常见 granite、gneiss、schist、sandstone、limestone、marl、loess 等。 ### Reading task 不要死背“Alsace 有多少种土壤”，而是理解：small geographic area + exceptional geological fragmentation = strong site identity。 ## 4｜Grape Varieties Alsace 与法国多数产区不同，酒标经常直接标示 grape variety。 ### Core white grapes - Riesling - Gewurztraminer - Pinot Gris - Muscat - Pinot Blanc / Auxerrois - Sylvaner ### Red - Pinot Noir ### Reading distinction Riesling / Gewurztraminer / Pinot Gris / Muscat 是 Grand Cru 学习中的核心“noble” varieties；但具体 Grand Cru permitted grapes 必须按各法规与例外理解。 ## 5｜Three Appellation Families ### Alsace AOP 区域性主体 appellation，可生产多种白、红、桃红及甜度风格。 ### Alsace Grand Cru AOP 由一组独立命名 Grand Cru sites 构成。学习重点不是只记“51”，而是理解：site-specific rules + permitted grape rules + stricter production standards。 ### Crémant d’Alsace AOP 传统法起泡酒；与 Module 06 cross-link。 ## 6｜Grand Cru Logic Alsace Grand Cru 强调 vineyard/site identity。多数 Grand Cru 以 Riesling、Gewurztraminer、Pinot Gris、Muscat family 为核心，但存在例外与 site-specific blending/variety rules。 ### Important reading principle 不要把 Alsace Grand Cru 当成 Burgundy Grand Cru 的同义制度。两者都强调 site，但历史、法规、葡萄、面积与市场逻辑不同。 ## 7｜Dry, Off-Dry & Sweet Styles Alsace 可以从完全干型到明显甜型。高成熟度年份、producer style 与 grape variety 都会影响最终甜度。 ### Late-harvest terms Vendanges Tardives (VT) = late harvest category。
Sélection de Grains Nobles (SGN) = selected noble-rotted / highly concentrated grapes，通常更甜、更浓缩。 ## 8｜Label Reading 学生看到 Alsace label 时，应依序识别： 1. Appellation 2. Grape 3. Grand Cru / lieu-dit / communal indication 4. VT / SGN 等甜酒术语 5. Producer 6. Vintage ## 9｜History — only what matters for wine Alsace 长期处于 French / German cultural interface，因此其葡萄品种、酒标语言、瓶型、饮食与酿酒文化带有明显跨境特征。 历史不是为了背战争时间表，而是为了理解：为什么一个法国 AOP 会如此“Germanic”地重视 varietal labels 与 aromatic white grapes。 ## 11｜Source Alignment Primary course/source base: - - - ## 12｜What is intentionally NOT here - Producer profiles - individual Grand Cru deep dives - maps beyond what is needed to read - historical trivia - further reading summaries - service expansion 这些全部留给 Understanding & Extension round。

title: 📖 06｜Core Text Reading · Other Sparkling Wines
text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/40617d16de4c81098c66e595ad3ec408 as of 2026-10-27T10:14:49.557Z: {"title":"06｜Core Text Reading · Other Sparkling Wines"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"📖"} Core Text Reading · Other Sparkling Wines
这一页只做 Reading：先读懂 production methods，再把 Cava / Crémant / Franciacorta / Trentodoc / Prosecco / Asti / Sekt / English Sparkling 等挂到方法上。 ## 1｜Start with the Method, not the Country Sparkling wine 最容易学乱，是因为学生先背产区名称。正确阅读顺序是：
How are bubbles created? → Where does secondary fermentation happen? → How long is lees contact? → What grape / region / style follows? ## 2｜Traditional Method Second fermentation occurs in bottle. The wine then ages on lees before riddling, disgorgement and dosage. ### What the method creates - finer, more integrated mousse - potential autolytic notes: bread / biscuit / brioche / toast - higher labour and production cost ### Core examples - Cava - Crémant - Franciacorta - Trentodoc - English Quality Sparkling - Cap Classique - premium Sekt / Winzersekt ## 3｜Tank Method / Charmat / Martinotti Second fermentation takes place in a pressurised tank rather than in the final bottle. ### Why use it? 更强调 primary fruit、floral aroma 与 freshness，减少长时间 lees ageing 带来的 autolysis。 ### Core examples - Prosecco - Asti / Moscato d’Asti production family - many Lambrusco - some Sekt ## 4｜Transfer Method Secondary fermentation first occurs in bottle, then wine is transferred under pressure to tank for finishing and rebottling. ### Reading point 它兼具 bottle fermentation 与 industrial efficiency；Certified 层认识概念即可。 ## 5｜Ancestral Method Wine is bottled before the first fermentation is complete, so fermentation finishes in bottle. ### Typical cues - one-fermentation logic - often lower pressure - may be cloudy / rustic depending producer - Pét-Nat and some traditional regional styles ## 6｜Carbonation CO₂ is injected into still wine. ### Reading point 这是最直接的制造气泡方式，通常最少 yeast-derived complexity。 ## 7｜Cava Spanish traditional-method sparkling wine. ### Core grapes - Macabeo - Xarel·lo - Parellada ### Reading focus 把 Cava 理解成 method + grape tradition + ageing categories + regional identity，不要只理解成“Spanish Champagne”。 ## 8｜Crémant Crémant 是法国多个不同 AOP 的 traditional-method sparkling family，而不是一个单独产区。 Examples: - Crémant d’Alsace - Crémant de Bourgogne - Crémant de Loire - Crémant de Limoux - Crémant du Jura - Crémant de Bordeaux ### Reading point 同样叫 Crémant，不代表葡萄品种和 regional style 相同。 ## 9｜Franciacorta Lombardia traditional-method sparkling. ### Core reading nodes - Chardonnay / Pinot Nero / permitted Pinot Bianco - Satèn - Rosé - Millesimato - Riserva Satèn = lower-pressure, softer-textured style within Franciacorta. ## 10｜Trentodoc Mountain traditional-method sparkling from Trentino. ### Reading connection Altitude + diurnal range → acidity + freshness → traditional-method structure。 ## 11｜Prosecco Production is generally tank-method focused. ### Core grape Glera ### Main hierarchy - Prosecco DOC - Asolo Prosecco DOCG - Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG ### Reading point Prosecco 的典型识别核心是 pear / apple / floral / fresh fruit—not long autolysis. ## 12｜Asti / Moscato d’Asti Based on Moscato Bianco. ### Core reading distinction 重点是 aromatic grape + sweetness + lower alcohol / pressure differences，而不是 bread/toast notes。 ## 13｜Sekt German-language sparkling wine category covering a wide quality range. Know the distinctions: - Sekt - Deutscher Sekt - Sekt b.A. - Winzersekt Premium examples often use traditional method and strong producer/site identity。 ## 14｜England, South Africa & Other New World Sparkling ### England Cool climate, high acidity, traditional method, Chardonnay / Pinot Noir / Meunier important. ### South Africa Cap Classique = traditional-method category. ### Australia / New Zealand / USA Cool-climate regions increasingly produce high-quality traditional-method sparkling wines. ## 15｜Method → Aroma Logic ### Traditional method bread / brioche / toast / biscuit / nut + finer mousse ### Tank method pear / apple / peach / grape / floral + brighter primary fruit ### Aromatic sparkling Moscato / Glera identity may be more obvious than autolysis. ## 16｜Service Reading For guest recommendation, a useful first question is:
“Do you want something fresh and fruity, or something more bready and complex?” That question maps directly to production method. ## 18｜Source Alignment - - - - ## 19｜What is intentionally NOT here No producer deep-dives, no law-heavy appendix, no map deep dive, no further-reading summaries. Those move to Understanding & Extension.

Reading only: DAC → region → Ried → grape → style. Keep Wachau and ÖTW as separate layers. ## 1｜Four Main Geographic Blocks Niederösterreich / Burgenland / Steiermark / Wien. ## 2｜Core Grapes Grüner Veltliner / Riesling / Blaufränkisch / Zweigelt / Sauvignon Blanc / Welschriesling. ## 3｜DAC Logic Read DAC as origin-based law.
Do not confuse DAC with private vineyard classifications or traditional style terms. ## 4｜Wachau Grüner Veltliner + Riesling.
Terraced Danube vineyards. Traditional style terms:
Steinfeder / Federspiel / Smaragd. These are not the same thing as the DAC origin hierarchy. ## 5｜Kamptal / Kremstal / Traisental / Weinviertel Grüner + Riesling dominate the reading.
Weinviertel is the classic Grüner Veltliner DAC anchor. ## 6｜Burgenland Blaufränkisch / Zweigelt + sweet-wine tradition. Key zones:
Leithaberg / Mittelburgenland / Eisenberg / Neusiedlersee / Rust. ## 7｜Ruster Ausbruch Historic noble-sweet style from Rust.
Botrytis + high acidity + lake influence. ## 8｜Steiermark Südsteiermark / Vulkanland Steiermark / Weststeiermark.
Sauvignon Blanc is a major modern identity.
Schilcher = rosé from Blauer Wildbacher. ## 9｜Wien Wiener Gemischter Satz = field-blend tradition. ## 10｜ÖTW Private association.
Erste Lage is a private site-classification concept, separate from DAC law. ## 12｜Source Alignment

Reading only: production → fermentation family → style → service; cider follows fruit → structure → region → service. ## 1｜Beer Raw Materials Water / malt / hops / yeast. ## 2｜Production Flow Mash → boil → ferment → condition → package. ## 3｜Ale & Lager Use ale/lager as broad fermentation families.
Do not reduce the distinction to a simplistic “top vs bottom” rule only; yeast behaviour, temperature and style tradition all matter. ## 4｜Core Beer Styles Pilsner / Helles / Kölsch / Weissbier / Saison / Belgian Dubbel / Tripel / Strong Ale / Pale Ale / IPA / Porter / Stout. ## 5｜Belgian Traditions Trappist is a certification/production context, not a beer style.
Abbey beer is not automatically Trappist. ## 6｜Lambic & Gueuze Spontaneous fermentation + aged hops + wood ageing/blending.
Gueuze = blended/refermented lambic tradition. ## 7｜Beer Service Correct glass / temperature / head / draft-line hygiene / bottle sediment / storage / freshness. ## 8｜Cider Apple varieties determine sugar / acid / tannin.
Styles may be still or sparkling, dry or sweet. ## 9｜Perry & Keeving Perry = pear-based fermented beverage.
Keeving is an important traditional cider-production concept. ## 10｜Regional Cider Anchors Normandy / Brittany / Basque Country / Asturias / England. ## 11｜Pairing Connection Beer bitterness / carbonation / malt and cider acidity / tannin make both useful with cheese, pork, spice and fried foods. ## 12｜Source Alignment Module 25｜Beer & Cider｜Stage 0–1 Deep Build

title: 📖 13｜Core Text Reading · Germany
text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/40617d16de4c81549855e6e504f8ea07 as of 2026-10-27T10:15:13.040Z: {"title":"13｜Core Text Reading · Germany"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"📖"} Core Text Reading · Germany
Reading only: official law → sweetness terms → VDP → regions → grapes → styles. ## 1｜Three Systems — Do Not Mix Them Germany must be read through three separate systems: 1. official wine law / Prädikat 2. sweetness language 3. VDP private origin classification ## 2｜Official Quality Framework Qualitätswein and Prädikatswein are the key quality-wine categories for this reading. Prädikat levels:
Kabinett / Spätlese / Auslese / Beerenauslese / Trockenbeerenauslese / Eiswein. ### Reading correction Prädikat is not the same as final sweetness. ## 3｜Sweetness Language Trocken / Halbtrocken / Feinherb / Lieblich / Süß. Understand the difference between a harvest/ripeness category and a finished-wine sweetness description. ## 4｜VDP Private association, not German state law. Gutswein → Ortswein → Erste Lage → Grosse Lage. Dry wine from a Grosse Lage = Grosses Gewächs / GG. ## 5｜Mosel Riesling + steep slate + Mosel/Saar/Ruwer.
Core villages/sites: Bernkastel / Wehlen / Graach / Ürzig / Piesport / Scharzhofberger. ## 6｜Rheingau Riesling + Spätburgunder.
South-facing Rhine slopes are a key spatial cue. ## 7｜Rheinhessen / Pfalz / Nahe Rheinhessen → Riesling renaissance, Roter Hang, Westhofen.
Pfalz → warmer/drier, Riesling + Pinot family.
Nahe → geological diversity + Riesling. ## 8｜Baden / Franken / Ahr Baden → Spätburgunder.
Franken → Silvaner + Bocksbeutel.
Ahr → Spätburgunder. ## 9｜Sweet Wine & Sekt BA / TBA / Eiswein.
Sekt / Deutscher Sekt / Sekt b.A. / Winzersekt. ## 11｜Source Alignment

title: 📖 28｜Core Text Reading · Deductive Tasting
text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/40617d16de4c81309c42f9fd693808b9 as of 2026-10-27T10:17:08.751Z: {"title":"28｜Core Text Reading · Deductive Tasting"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"📖"} Core Text Reading · Deductive Tasting
Reading only: observation → structure → evidence → conclusion. No blind-tasting questions inside the reading layer. ## 1｜Purpose of Deduction Deductive tasting is a structured way to turn sensory observations into a reasoned wine conclusion. ## 2｜Sight Clarity / brightness / colour / concentration / rim variation / viscosity / evidence of gas or sediment. ## 3｜Nose Condition / intensity / age development / fruit / floral / herbal / spice / earth / oak / fermentation and maturation cues. ## 4｜Palate Sweetness / acid / tannin / alcohol / body / flavour intensity / texture / finish. ## 5｜Structure Before Identity Acid, tannin, alcohol and body are more reliable anchors than a single aroma association. ## 6｜Climate & Ripeness Cues Fruit ripeness, alcohol, acidity and phenolic maturity can suggest climate and growing conditions, but none should be used alone. ## 7｜Winemaking Cues Oak / lees / malolactic / extraction / carbonic or semi-carbonic context / oxidation / reduction may shape the profile. ## 8｜Old World / New World Use geographic-style language carefully.
Do not treat “Old World” and “New World” as rigid sensory categories. ## 9｜Conclusion Logic Evidence should move from:
grape/style family → climate → region possibilities → quality/age → final conclusion. ## 10｜Tasting Discipline Describe first, interpret second.
Avoid changing observations simply to force a preferred conclusion. ## 11｜Core Connection sensory evidence → structure → production/climate → grape/style → origin → conclusion. ## 12｜Source Alignment Module 28｜Deductive Tasting｜Stage 0–1 Deep Build

title: 📖 12｜Core Text Reading · Italy
text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/40617d16de4c81fbab05dc6ba8db92b9 as of 2026-10-27T10:15:10.416Z: {"title":"12｜Core Text Reading · Italy"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"📖"} Core Text Reading · Italy
Italy reading should be national framework first, then regional anchors. Do not begin by memorising every DOCG. ## 1｜National Framework Read the legal categories:
DOCG / DOC / IGT / Vino. Understand that legal category and absolute wine quality are not the same thing. ## 2｜Label Language Classico / Riserva / Superiore / Vigna / Passito / Appassimento / Recioto / Ripasso. These words recur across Italy but their exact legal meaning is appellation-specific. ## 3｜Piemonte Nebbiolo → Barolo / Barbaresco.

Zinfandel is synonymous with California, although it came from the Primitivo grape in Italy and its older origins are reputed to be in Croatia. 丹魄（Tempranillo）是用于里奥哈（Rioja）和纳瓦拉（Navarra）葡萄酒的主要葡萄品种，在西班牙许多其他地区也有种植。它是阿根廷的重要品种，也是波特酒生产中使用最多的品种之一，在当地被称为罗丽红（Tinta Roriz）。这类葡萄酒酒体饱满，带有樱桃、草莓和覆盆子的风味。国产多瑞加（Touriga Nacional）是波特酒混酿中最重要的优质品种，同时也酿出一些出色的强劲红葡萄酒。这些葡萄酒核心呈近乎黑色的深邃色泽，充满黑色水果风味，单宁和酸度较高。当该葡萄在混酿中占主要比例时，所酿出的静态葡萄酒品质最佳。仙粉黛（Zinfandel）是加利福尼亚的代名词，尽管它源自意大利的普里米蒂沃（Primitivo）葡萄，而其更古老的起源据信位于克罗地亚。 It is the most planted red grape in California, and much of it is made into a sweet rosé wine known as blush wine or white Zinfandel. The more serious Zinfandels are deep-coloured, with jammy red and black plummy fruit characters, medium-high tannins, high acid and high alcohol. These red Zinfandels lend themselves to oak maturation. 它是加利福尼亚种植最广泛的红葡萄品种，其中大部分被酿造成一种名为“淡红酒”或“白仙粉黛”的甜型桃红葡萄酒。更为优质的仙粉黛红酒色泽深邃，带有果酱般的红色与黑色李子风味，单宁中高，酸度和酒精度均较高。这类红葡萄酒适合进行橡木桶陈酿。 ### Terms & Context｜术语与背景 Book｜pp.43–48 这一部分不要当作“背 30 个品种香气”的章节。它真正的用途是给后面的 Regions + Tasting 打基础。 ### White grapes｜白葡萄 - Chardonnay： 气候、MLF、lees、oak 对风格影响特别明显。 - Sauvignon Blanc： 常见清新酸度，可从柑橘/草本到更成熟热带果味。 - Riesling / Chenin Blanc： 高酸与不同甜度可以同时存在。 - Gewürztraminer / Muscat： 芳香强，不代表一定甜。 - Pinot Gris/Grigio / Viognier： 用来练习果味、酒体、酸度与成熟度关系。 ### Red grapes｜红葡萄 - Pinot Noir / Gamay： 颜色可以较浅；结构不能只看颜色。 - Cabernet Sauvignon / Cabernet Franc： 成熟度会改变果香与草本表现。 - Merlot / Malbec： 不要背成固定“低单宁”或固定香气。 - Syrah / Grenache： 从香料、果味、颜色、酒精、酸和结构比较。 - Nebbiolo / Sangiovese： 很适合说明浅色 ≠ 低单宁。 Advanced note · Variety thinking 从现在开始训练：Variety → climate → ripeness → winemaking → structure → likely regions。这是 Certified 往 Advanced 过渡最有价值的一步，比背孤立香气词有效得多。 --- # 15 · Must-Know Wine Terms｜本章重点术语
Term 中文 What you need to know
Terroir 风土 环境与栽培因素的相互作用，不等于土壤。
Aspect 坡向 影响太阳辐射，需要结合南北半球。
Véraison 转色期 成熟开始，果粒软化并发生颜色变化。
Buttage 培土 在葡萄藤基部堆土，用于保护与栽培管理。
Passerillage 干缩 葡萄失水后糖分与成分浓缩。
Scion 接穗 嫁接上部结果品种。
Rootstock 砧木 根系部分，提供抗性/适应性。
Triage 分选 酒庄挑选健康、合适原料。
Cuvaison 带皮浸渍/发酵期 红酒果皮与发酵液接触的阶段。
Vin de goutte 自流酒 从红酒发酵罐自然流出的酒液。
Vin de presse 压榨酒 压榨皮渣得到的酒液。
Chaptalisation 加糖增醇 添加可发酵糖提高潜在酒精，不等于增甜。
Mutage 加烈止酵 发酵中加烈，保留部分葡萄糖。
Pigeage 压帽 把酒帽压入发酵液。
Remontage 淋皮 抽出酒液再泵淋酒帽。
Macération carbonique 二氧化碳浸渍 完整果粒先发生细胞内代谢。
MLF 苹果酸乳酸发酵 苹果酸→乳酸；通常降低酸感。
Sur lie 酒泥陈酿 让酒与酒泥接触熟成。
Bâtonnage 搅酒泥 搅动并重新悬浮酒泥。
Soutirage 换桶/转罐 将酒从沉淀中转移到另一容器。
Tartrates 酒石结晶 酒石酸盐晶体，通常无害。
--- # 16 · After Reading｜读完这一章你应该能做到 - [ ] 不看资料解释 climate / aspect / water / ripeness 的关系。 - [ ] 解释 grafting / scion / rootstock / phylloxera。 - [ ] 说出 vine cycle，并解释 frost、flowering、véraison、harvest 的风险。 - [ ] 画出典型 white vs red vinification。 - [ ] 区分 crushing vs pressing。 - [ ] 区分 pigeage / remontage / delestage。 - [ ] 区分 alcoholic fermentation vs MLF。 - [ ] 解释 lees / sur lie / bâtonnage / oak regime。 - [ ] 正确解释六个 Certified 法语重点：buttage, passerillage, véraison, mutage, pigeage, remontage。 - [ ] 能在基础概念之上解释相关因果，而不只是背定义。 ## Extension｜想继续往下读

Source base： Brian K. Julyan, Sales and Service for the Wine Professional, Fifth Edition, Chapter 2, printed pp.27–48.

Reading only: build a pairing decision framework, not memorised food = wine rules. ## 1｜Start with the Dish Structure Read the dish through:
intensity / dominant taste / sauce / cooking method / fat-protein / spice / sweetness / texture. ## 2｜Acidity Wine acidity refreshes fat and salt.
An acidic dish can make a low-acid wine feel flat. ## 3｜Sweetness For desserts, the wine should generally be at least as sweet as the dish.
Residual sugar can soften chilli heat. ## 4｜Tannin Protein and fat can soften tannin perception.
Bitterness and chilli can make tannin feel harsher. ## 5｜Alcohol Higher alcohol amplifies chilli heat and warmth. ## 6｜Salt & Umami Salt can soften bitterness and tannin.
Umami can make wine seem more bitter/astringent, so fruit, acidity or sweetness may help. ## 7｜Cooking Method Raw / steamed / grilled / roasted / braised / fried / smoked change the dish’s intensity and aroma. ## 8｜Sauce First Sauce, garnish and seasoning often influence pairing more strongly than the protein itself. ## 9｜Cheese Fresh / soft-ripened / hard / blue / washed-rind differ in salt, fat and intensity and therefore need different wine structures. ## 10｜Restaurant Recommendation Logic Guest preference, budget, sweetness tolerance and adventurousness should shape the recommendation.
Technical knowledge must be translated into clear guest language. ## 11｜Core Connection dish → taste/texture → wine structure → region/style → service temperature/glass ## 12｜Source Alignment Module 26｜Food & Wine Pairing｜Stage 0–1 Deep Build
